provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Auto family batch. Niche, loyal riders and almost no web presence, so copy is enthusiast-facing and season-driven. Machines and parts described by type, never by manufacturer. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.section: Trailer axle, brake and wiring service
pageStructurePlus.contains: Wheel bearing repacks, electric and surge brakes, breakaway switches, lights and wiring harnesses, leaf springs, couplers and safety chains for utility, boat and car-hauler trailers
pageStructurePlus.why: Trailer owners search the failed part, a light that won't work or a hot hub. A page that names each trailer job gets the call before the trip.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Winterizing motorcycles, ATVs, side-by-sides and RVs, fuel stabilizer, battery tenders, plumbing antifreeze for campers, indoor storage and spring de-winterize
pageStructurePlus.why: Storage and winterization lock in the spring tune-up. Riders book the shop that makes the off-season one appointment.

pageStructurePlus.section: Pickup and delivery for bikes and machines
pageStructurePlus.contains: Picking up a motorcycle, ATV or side-by-side that won't run, hauling trailers that can't be towed safely, delivery fees by distance, and loading straps and soft ties
pageStructurePlus.why: A dead quad in a barn can't get to the shop. Pickup is often the deciding factor, and it deserves its own page.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Carburetor cleaning and rebuilds, two-stroke top ends, older dirt bikes and classic motorcycles, discontinued parts sourcing, and what the shop won't take on
pageStructurePlus.why: Many dealers turn away older machines. Riders with a project bike search for the independent powersports shop that will touch it.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Spring motorcycle tune-ups, hunting-season ATV checks, track-day prep, tire and chain service, and a trip checklist for camper and toy-hauler trailers
pageStructurePlus.why: Demand spikes at season start. A pre-season page books the work weeks earlier and spreads the rush.

pageStructurePlus.section: RV roof, slide-out and appliance repair
pageStructurePlus.contains: Roof reseal and leak repair, slide-out mechanisms, water heaters, furnaces, fridges and generators, plus mobile RV service at the campsite or driveway
pageStructurePlus.why: RV owners need a repair shop that can take a big rig or come to it. A separate RV page stops them assuming it's motorcycles only.

designDirections.name: Trail Ready
designDirections.bestFor: One-shop powersports mechanics who sell on a fast repair request and pickup for machines that won't run
designDirections.headlineSample: ATV, motorcycle and trailer repair in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: Basalt and lime read like trail gear and hi-vis, and the geometric caps keep the request button loud on a phone in the garage.

designDirections.name: Garage Builds
designDirections.bestFor: Shops with motorcycle rebuilds, side-by-side builds and restored trailers worth showing off
designDirections.whyItFits: The family combo. Riders follow builds, and a near-black gallery makes chrome, engine cases and mud-caked machines look like the magazine shots they collect.

designDirections.name: Fleet Trailer Bay
designDirections.bestFor: Shops servicing trailer fleets for landscapers, contractors, equipment rental yards and dealers
designDirections.headlineSample: Trailer fleet service and inspections in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: Steel blue on white reads like an inspection sheet. Fleet managers compare capacity, turnaround and records, not mood.

openers.line: Your powersports shop has loyal reviews on Maps but no website. Someone in {City} with a quad that won't idle can't see whether you work on their machine before they call.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there's no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: What could sit behind that button for the shop: {demo-link}

openers.line: Most of what I can find about your shop is shout-outs in local riding groups. That's great word of mouth, and a rider new to town still has nowhere to see what you fix or how to book.
openers.hook: Search their shop name in local riding or trail Facebook groups. Note a recent shout-out.
openers.linkLine: Where those riding-group shout-outs would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: The site on your listing still shows a winter-hours notice and no mention of trailers or side-by-sides. A rider comparing motorcycle shops reads that as a place that's slowed down.
openers.hook: Open the site and look for stale notices, missing services or an old copyright year. Note which.

openers.angle: Site hard to use in the garage
openers.line: On my phone your shop site's service list was a wall of text with no tap-to-call. Riders look you up standing next to the dead bike in the garage, phone in one greasy hand.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on a phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: A motorcycle and ATV shop page built for a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: There's no way to send your shop the machine, the year and what it's doing without calling. A request form for ATVs, bikes and trailers lets you sort the carb cleans from the engine jobs before they show up.
openers.hook: Check the listing and social pages for a request form. If there's none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A repair request built for bikes, ATVs and trailers: {demo-link}

openers.line: That side-by-side build and the restored dirt bike on your page are the kind of work riders drive an hour for. They're buried between parts-arrival posts.
openers.hook: Find two builds or rebuilds you can name by machine type and work done. Mention one if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your powersports builds on their own page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews keep saying you fixed a machine the dealer wouldn't touch. That one line is the whole reason a rider with an older bike would pick your shop.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one line about an older machine, a fair price or speed. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Those reviews next to the machines you fix: {demo-link}

openers.line: When the first warm weekend hits {City}, every rider wants their motorcycle running and every camper owner hitches up a trailer with dead lights. The shops riders can book online fill first.
openers.hook: Use in late winter. Name the season or the local trail opening in the reply.
openers.linkLine: A pre-season tune-up page ready before riding season: {demo-link}

openers.line: Riders find out the machine won't start on Saturday morning, when your shop might be closed. A request form catches that ATV or bike before they take it to the dealer on Monday.
openers.hook: Check their listed hours. If they close weekends or evenings, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A weekend repair request for riders: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're looking for a powersports tech. Good mechanics who love bikes check out a shop's builds and setup online before they apply.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note. Note the date and role.
openers.linkLine: A powersports shop page with a careers section: {demo-link}

openers.line: Riders bring machines from all over around {City}, but nothing tells someone out in {Neighborhood} whether you'll pick up a dead ATV or what that costs. That's their first question.
openers.hook: Find towns or trail areas mentioned in posts or reviews. Use the furthest one.
openers.linkLine: A pickup-and-delivery page for bikes and trailers: {demo-link}

openers.line: If you split engine rebuilds or RV roof jobs into payments, say so on the page. A big repair is when riders decide whether to fix the machine or sell it as-is.
openers.hook: Only if they mention payment options somewhere. If not, skip this angle.
openers.linkLine: Bigger powersports repairs with payments explained: {demo-link}

openers.line: Leaving a motorcycle or camper at a shop for a few weeks makes people nervous. A page that covers your storage, security and insurance answers that before they hand over the keys.
openers.hook: Look for any mention of indoor storage, security or insurance. Never state coverage they didn't publish.
openers.linkLine: Storage, security and insurance on one shop page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Sounds like your shop runs on riders telling riders. That's the best kind of work, and the friend who gets your name still searches before trailering a machine over.
openers.hook: Look for reviews like 'my riding buddy sent me'. Quote one back.
openers.linkLine: Where a rider's referral to your shop would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw the {specific recent job} on your page. Riders hunting for a powersports mechanic who can handle that kind of work would trailer an hour for it, if they could find it.
openers.hook: Pick the newest repair or build post and name it exactly: machine type, problem and what was done.

sequence.dm1:
Hey {Owner} — that {specific recent job} you posted is serious wrenching.

I looked for powersports and trailer repair in {City} and found {Business Name} through riding-group shout-outs, but no site where someone can send their machine and book. I put together a sample shop page for bikes, ATVs and trailers, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Want me to send it over?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner} — following up in case my last message got buried. Here's the sample site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has a repair request for motorcycles, ATVs, side-by-sides and trailers, a winterization and storage page, pickup and delivery, and a page for older carbureted machines. If it's not for you, say so and I'll leave you be.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for powersports and trailer shops here in {City}. I sent you a message a couple of days ago, did it come through?"

IF NO:
"Short version: I built a sample site for {Business Name} with a repair request for bikes, ATVs and trailers, a winterization page and pickup details, with marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I text you the link?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range} depending on how many machine and service pages you want, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and changes. For a shop your size I'd quote about {Build Price}, about one top-end rebuild."
"Can I walk you through it for ten minutes this week?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and an invoice for the deposit. We start the day it clears."

objections.objection: Riders find me through word of mouth.
objections.handler: "They do, and they still search your name before trailering a machine over. The site is where a riding buddy's recommendation lands."

objections.objection: I'm backed up for weeks already.
objections.handler: "Then the request form helps most. You see the machine and the problem first, book the quick carb cleans in gaps and quote the rebuilds properly."
"That's when winterization and storage sell, and when the site gets found before spring. It's working the day riding season starts."

objections.objection: The dealers get all the online traffic.
objections.handler: "Dealers turn away older machines and trailers. A page that says your shop takes them is exactly what those riders search for."

objections.objection: My cousin can put up a page for me.
objections.handler: "Good, that's cheaper. I'll hand over the request form and the winterization page I built. If it stalls before spring, the offer stands."
"{Build Range}. For your shop about {Build Price}: repair request, machine pages, winterization and pickup. Roughly one rebuild."

email.subject: Powersports shop site for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "{Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for powersports and trailer shops in {City}, and put together a sample for {Business Name}. I'll text you the link. Have a look when the shop's quiet. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner} — I'm taking the {Business Name} powersports demo down on Friday to free up the space.

Want me to leave it up? One word is fine either way.
sequence.nurture:
Hey {Owner} — riding season is a few weeks out and every bike and trailer in {City} is about to need a tune-up at once. Thought of you.

The site is still here whenever you want it, and nothing's changed on price. {demo-link} if you want another look.

bullets: Peg the build to roughly one engine rebuild, never to an hourly rate.
Price each machine type page separately: motorcycles, ATVs and side-by-sides, trailers and RVs answer different searches.
A repair request that asks machine type, year and symptom is the core product. Charge for it as its own line.
Winterization and storage pages pay back in one season; put them in the first scope for shops in cold climates.
Only quote RV pages for shops that can fit an RV or do mobile RV service.
Fleet trailer pages are a separate line for shops near contractors and rental yards.

lineItems.description: Max with machine type, year, symptom, running-or-not, pickup needed and photo upload.
Max when the page lists common jobs, the shop's builds for that machine type and a booking link.
Max with package options by machine, storage capacity, pickup scheduling and a spring de-winterize booking.
Max with distance-based fees, a map, loading notes and trailer-tow requests.

lineItems.item: RV repair and mobile service page
lineItems.description: Max with separate roof, slide-out and appliance sections and a mobile campsite request form.
Max with a unit-list upload, inspection checklist and scheduled yard visits.

whatElseYouSell.name: Shop build video and photo day
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "One day filming a motorcycle teardown, a side-by-side on the lift and a trailer brake job gives riders the build content they actually follow."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, when a build is mid-way on the bench.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile management for powersports work
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Weekly posts of ATVs, bikes and trailers you fixed, with the machine type and the town, so 'atv repair near me' finds your shop."
whatElseYouSell.when: Day 30, once the site is live.

whatElseYouSell.name: Review requests at machine pickup
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "When the rider loads up the fixed machine, they get a text with a review link. Reviews about bikes the dealer wouldn't touch sell your shop."

whatElseYouSell.name: Fall winterization campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A push in the fall for motorcycle, ATV and camper winterization, sent to past customers first, fills the storage bays and books spring."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in August, run September and October.

whatElseYouSell.name: Trail and riding-group sponsorship kit
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A banner, stickers and a QR card for the local trail cleanup or ride day, so every rider there knows the powersports shop that sponsors it."
whatElseYouSell.when: Before the first group ride of the season.

whatElseYouSell.name: Spring tune-up reminder mailer
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A postcard and text to every rider who stored or winterized with you: book the spring tune-up before the trails open."

withoutAI.route: Trailer sales lots that need a service partner
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The trailer lot you fix warranty brakes for needs an inventory site. Your shop goes on it as their service partner."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Trailer dealers rarely have service bays and need a trusted shop on their site.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The RV park whose guests call you for slide-outs and water heaters needs a site that books campsites. Your mobile RV service is on it."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Campgrounds buy booking sites and want a repair partner for guests.

withoutAI.whoPays: The club, from dues or sponsors
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The trail club you sponsor runs on a group chat. A site with trail conditions, rides and a sponsor wall puts your shop in front of every member."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Clubs need a home and sponsors; the shop owner is already involved.

withoutAI.whoPays: The marine mechanic, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "When a rider asks about their boat motor, who do you send them to? That marine mechanic has the same no-website problem."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Powersports and marine customers overlap heavily and trade referrals.

withoutAI.route: Equipment rental yards with trailer fleets
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The rental yard whose trailers you keep road-ready needs a rental booking site. Your trailer service keeps it running."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Rental yards have budget and already depend on the shop for trailer upkeep.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The outfitter whose ATVs you prep every fall needs a site to book hunts. Your shop keeps their machines on the trail."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Outfitters buy booking sites and trust the mechanic who preps their fleet.

withAI.route: Trailer buyer's question assistant for the dealer
withAI.pitchLine: "Buyers ask the trailer lot about payload, brakes and hitch class at night. An assistant answers from the dealer's specs and books service with your shop."
withAI.whyItWorks: Dealers lose sales to slow answers. The shop gets routed service.

withAI.route: Campsite and repair booking assistant for the RV park
withAI.pitchLine: "Guests ask about sites, hookups and 'my water heater quit'. An assistant books the site and hands RV repair requests to your mobile service."
withAI.whyItWorks: Campground offices are small and swamped in season.

withAI.route: Trail conditions summary for the riding club
withAI.pitchLine: "Members post trail reports in the chat; an assistant drafts a weekly trail conditions summary for the club site, sponsored by your shop."
withAI.whyItWorks: Clubs want current trail info and sponsors want visibility.

withAI.pitchLine: "Missed calls get a text asking for the motor, hours and where the boat is stored. Same text-back setup as the powersports shop."
withAI.whyItWorks: Second build is configuration on a warm referral.

withAI.route: Rental return damage notes for the rental yard
withAI.pitchLine: "Returned trailers get a damage check from return pictures, drafted for staff to confirm, with repairs routed to your trailer shop."
withAI.whyItWorks: Rental yards argue over damage constantly. The shop gets the repair work.

withAI.route: Hunt booking assistant for the outfitter
withAI.pitchLine: "Hunters ask about dates, lodging and whether ATVs are provided. An assistant answers from the outfitter's packages and books the hunt."
withAI.whyItWorks: Outfitters run on phone and email. The powersports client makes the introduction.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back that asks for the machine
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A missed call gets a text asking for machine type, year and what it's doing. You call back knowing it's a trailer light, not a motorcycle top end."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs the shop number forwarded and the wording they approve.

softwareAI.name: Ready-for-pickup and storage texts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Riders get a text when the bike or ATV is ready, and a storage-fee reminder if it sits in the powersports shop too long."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their storage policy and job stages.

softwareAI.name: Winterization signup with spring auto-booking
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Riders pick a winterization package for each machine, schedule pickup, and get the spring de-winterize booked in the same step."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: August. Needs their packages, storage capacity and pickup rules.

softwareAI.name: Service price list by machine type
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Starting prices for motorcycle tune-ups, ATV carb cleans, trailer bearing repacks and RV roof reseals, each with a request button."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their real starting prices for common jobs.

softwareAI.name: Symptom intake assistant for riders
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A rider types 'quad bogs when I hit the throttle' and the assistant asks fuel, sitting time and carb questions, then books the repair with notes."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their intake questions and services. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Pickup scheduling and route
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Dead bikes, ATVs and trailers needing pickup land on one route by area, with fees calculated and loading notes attached."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their pickup fees and truck-and-trailer capacity.

softwareAI.name: Rider-voice review replies
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A rider thanks the shop for saving an old two-stroke; a reply that talks about that exact dirt bike is drafted for the owner to tweak and post."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs ten past replies. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Parts finder for older machines
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Type the machine and the part, and it searches the shop's supplier lists and past orders for carb kits and gaskets on discontinued models."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs supplier price lists and past part orders. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Storage bay inventory board
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every stored motorcycle, ATV and camper with its bay, battery-tender status and spring date, so nothing gets lost in a packed winter shop."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, before storage season. Needs their bay layout and current storage list.

softwareAI.name: Trailer fleet inspection log
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each fleet trailer gets an inspection record: brakes, bearings, lights, tires, with the next due date sent to the fleet manager."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, when a fleet account signs. Needs the unit list and inspection checklist.

softwareAI.name: Bench notes to invoice writer
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The mechanic talks through the motorcycle or ATV job on the bench: jets cleaned, float set, new plug. It drafts the invoice and the rider's summary."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their invoice template and labor rates. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Spring tune-up booking wave
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Late winter, riders get tune-up invites in batches so the spring rush spreads across weeks instead of one Saturday."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: January. Needs their customer list and daily capacity.

softwareAI.name: Build log pages for project machines
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each big rebuild gets a private page where the owner sees progress pictures and parts as the bike or side-by-side comes together."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs a phone on the bench and their build stages.

softwareAI.name: Caption writer for build posts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Drop the build clip and notes, and it drafts a caption riders like: machine, problem, fix and a request link."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs twenty past captions. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: RV mobile service request triage
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Camper owners describe the leak or dead fridge, and the assistant sorts what can be fixed at the campsite from what needs the RV in the shop."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, for shops doing RV work. Needs their mobile service rules. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Season-end maintenance reminders
softwareAI.pitchLine: "After hunting season or the last trail ride, owners get a reminder for chain, oil and storage prep on their machine."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs customer machine list and season dates.

softwareAI.name: Job costing by machine type
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See whether motorcycles, ATVs, trailers or RVs actually make the shop money once parts hunting and bench time are counted."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs a season of invoices and labor hours.

softwareAI.name: Rider service history portal
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Riders see every repair on each machine they own, handy when selling a bike or trailer with records."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 8. Needs past invoices per customer.

softwareAI.name: Win-back notes for lapsed riders
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Riders who skipped a season get a short note drafted from their last service and machine, with a tune-up link."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 8, with a year of history. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Powersports tech applicant screener
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Applicants answer questions on two-stroke, four-stroke, trailer and RV experience before the owner calls."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Any time they post a hiring note. Needs their must-haves. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A repair request that knows ATVs, bikes, trailers and RVs is what every small powersports shop is missing. Almost none have a site."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Niche with almost no web presence. The first shop taught you the machine questions.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Dealer locator for a powersports parts distributor
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Riders search for a shop that can fix their machine. A locator of independent shops buying your parts sends them work."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Distributors want shop loyalty. Sending riders beats discounts.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your trailer buyers need warranty service near them. A network page routes them to approved independent repair shops."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Trailer makers rarely run service; they need partners and a locator.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A member directory of trusted repair shops, trail info and ride calendars, built on what one powersports shop already uses."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations want member value and shop sponsors. One deal reaches many riders and shops.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Agencies picking up motorcycle and ATV shops can license my template with the machine request and winterization built in."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies sell; you supply the niche build.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every rental branch's trailers inspected and repaired by approved local shops, tracked in one portal."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Rental companies need road-ready trailers everywhere. Local shops are the supply.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "RV parks across the region list mobile RV repair partners, so guests with a dead water heater get help without leaving the site."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Campground groups want guest services; RV techs want steady calls.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "An owner running shops in two trail towns needs one brand with a page and request routing per location."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Consolidation in niche shops is rising. One template, many locations.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Outfitter and guide fleet maintenance program
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Outfitters across the region get pre-season ATV and trailer prep scheduled with approved shops in one plan."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Outfitters can't afford breakdowns mid-season. Shops get steady fall work.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A short monthly sheet on what independent powersports shops charge for common jobs, built only from rates owners share."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Niche shops price blind. Contributed data keeps it honest.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Own the next trail town's shop
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: A powersports shop in another metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "One powersports and trailer shop per region on my list. You're the {City} shop; the next trail town over has nobody online at all."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Easy to own a whole metro. The template and proof travel.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A rider buddy started your shop site and stopped at the home page. I finish it on a powersports template that already takes machine requests."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Owners with half-built sites already decided to spend.

upsellLadder.offer: Powersports shop site build plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo.
upsellLadder.line: "The powersports site and the care plan go on one contract, so new winter hours or a trailer service is a text to me."

upsellLadder.trigger: The first machines from site requests are picked up.
upsellLadder.line: "Those first riders from the site rolled their bikes out happy. Let's get every one into a review."

upsellLadder.offer: Shop build video and photo day
upsellLadder.trigger: A standout rebuild is on the bench, or the gallery has only a few machines.
upsellLadder.line: "That side-by-side rebuild on the bench is the shoot. One day fills the gallery and a month of rider posts."

upsellLadder.trigger: Riders start asking about winter storage, or fall is a month out.
upsellLadder.line: "Storage questions are starting. A winterization signup fills the bays and books every spring tune-up at once."

upsellLadder.trigger: Request data shows vague 'won't start' requests the shop calls back about.
upsellLadder.line: "Most ATV and bike requests say 'won't run'. The intake asks the fuel and sitting-time questions first."

upsellLadder.trigger: Storage fills past half the bays, or a machine gets misplaced.
upsellLadder.line: "The storage bays are packed. A board shows every stored bike and camper and its spring date."

upsellLadder.trigger: A landscaper or rental yard asks the shop to service several trailers.
upsellLadder.line: "That landscaper's trailers are a standing account. An inspection log makes it professional and recurring."
